docs.title: Architecture, Request Flow, Auth & Permissions
docs.text: AI-context reference. Read AGENTS.md first for project overview and the load-bearing gotchas. This file covers request pipeline, JWT auth, and the PermissionMatrix authorisation model.

docs.title: Settings modes
docs.text:
Settings live in ad4x4/settings.py. The mode is selected by whether DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is present in the environment:

  • Production — DJANGO_SECRET_KEY env var present → PostgreSQL, Redis, SSL enforced, email SMTP, Bugsink.
  • Development — env var absent → SQLite or local Postgres (via DEV_DB_* vars), in-memory cache, console email, Huey immediate mode (tasks run synchronously).

docs.title: Request pipeline
docs.text:
Client (Flutter app / web)
  → HTTPS → nginx (reverse proxy, SSL termination)
  → Gunicorn (WSGI, prod) / manage.py runserver (dev)
  → Django middleware stack (in order):
      SecurityMiddleware → SessionMiddleware → CorsMiddleware → CommonMiddleware
      → CsrfViewMiddleware → AuthenticationMiddleware → MessageMiddleware
      → XFrameOptionsMiddleware → WhitenoiseMiddleware
      → CamelCaseMiddleWare        ← converts snake_case ↔ camelCase
      → CharsetMiddleware           ← adds charset=utf-8 to responses
      → MediaCorsMiddleware         ← CORS wildcard for /uploads/ and /media/
      → LastVisitedMiddleware       ← updates Member.last_visited (throttled 1/hr)
  → DRF authentication:
      JWTAuthentication (custom HS256, see Auth section below)
      → SessionAuthentication (fallback)
  → DRF permission classes (per-view)
  → ViewSet / APIView
  → Service layer (api/services/)
  → Models / ORM
  → PostgreSQL

docs.title: CamelCase conversion (critical)
docs.text: All JSON in and out is camelCase — handled automatically by djangorestframework_camel_case. Write snake_case internally; clients always see camelCase. Only exceptions: password1 and password2 (excluded via JSON_UNDERSCOREIZE).

docs.title: Response envelope
docs.text:
// Success
{"success": true, "message": {...}}

// Error
{"success": false, "message": "error description or validation dict"}

// Warning requiring explicit client confirmation before mutation
{"success": false, "message": "trip_overlap_warning", "warnings": [...]}

// Paginated list
{"count": 100, "next": "url", "previous": "url", "results": [...]}

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Default 10 per page. Client can pass page_size up to 500.

docs.title: Throttling
docs.text:
• Anonymous: 100 req/min
  • Authenticated: 200 req/min

docs.title: Authentication & JWT
docs.text: Library: djangorestframework-simplejwt with the token_blacklist app enabled. Header: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. Algorithm: HS256 signed with SECRET_KEY.

docs.title: Token lifetimes (env-overridable)
docs.text:
• Access token: 24 hours (ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES, default 1440)
  • Refresh token: 30 days (REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS, default 30)

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text: ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS=True + BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION=True. Every successful /api/token/refresh/ call returns a new refresh token and blacklists the old one. Reusing the same refresh token twice returns 401. Clients must overwrite their stored refresh token with the response value.

docs.title: Token payload
docs.text: token_type, exp, iat, jti, user_id. No token_version check (legacy).

docs.title: Custom classes
docs.text:
• api.util.JWTAuthentication — thin simplejwt subclass. Overrides get_user() only to preserve the legacy side effect of touching NotificationSettings on every authenticated request.
  • api.views.views_auth.LoginView — custom login mounted at /api/auth/login/ before rest_registration's URL include. Accepts login / username / email (case-insensitive on all) + password, returns {access, refresh} via RefreshToken.for_user(user) wrapped in the unified envelope.
  • api.views.views_auth.UnifiedTokenObtainPairView / UnifiedTokenRefreshView — wrappers around simplejwt's stock views that return the unified envelope. Mounted at /api/token/ and /api/token/refresh/.
  • api.views.views_auth.LogoutView, LogoutAllView, SessionsView — session management (see below).
  • api.views.views_auth.CustomChangePasswordView — see the gotcha in AGENTS.md: blacklists every refresh token for the user after set_password.

docs.title: Login fields
docs.text: login, username, or email (any of them, case-insensitive) plus password. The same case-insensitive lookup is reused by find_user_case_insensitive_by_send_reset_password_link_data for reset-password.

docs.title: Default permission
docs.text: IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly (safe methods public by default unless a view overrides).

docs.title: Member.token_version
docs.text: Legacy, unused. Column still on the model but nothing reads or writes it. Slated for removal. Do not reintroduce checks.

docs.title: Invalidation semantics
docs.text: Action Scope Mechanism POST /api/auth/logout/ Only the session whose refresh token is in the request body .blacklist() on that one JTI DELETE /api/auth/sessions/ (with keep_refresh) All sessions except the one whose refresh token is supplied .blacklist() on every other JTI POST /api/auth/logout-all/ Every session including the current one .blacklist() on every JTI for the user POST /api/auth/change-password/ Every session including the current one _blacklist_all_user_tokens(user) after set_password Refresh token rotated on use Previous refresh JTI invalidated, new one issued BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION=True handles it Refresh token expires naturally That one session simplejwt rejects on exp check, no DB work

docs.title: Permission system
docs.text: PermissionMatrix is the authoritative authorisation model. Django Groups + PermissionMatrix records together drive every protected action.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Each PermissionMatrix row maps a (group, action) pair.
  2. If levels M2M is empty, the permission applies to all member levels (this is the opposite of what you might expect — see AGENTS.md gotchas).
  3. If levels is specified, the permission applies only when the target member is at one of those levels.
  4. PermissionMatrix.has_permission(user, action, member=None, trip=None, require_trip_lead=False) is the single authoritative check.

docs.title: Every protected view must add a PermissionMatrix check
docs.text: When writing a new view that exposes a protected action you must explicitly add PermissionMatrix.has_permission() — do not assume one exists. Do not use Django model-level perms (is_staff, is_superuser) for business logic; those are admin-panel shortcuts only. The rule is not just "don't bypass it" — it's "always add it to every view that needs it."

docs.title: ActionChoice values (key ones)
docs.text:
CREATE_TRIP, CREATE_TRIP_WITH_APPROVAL, APPROVE_TRIP
EDIT_TRIPS, EDIT_TRIP_MEDIA, EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS, DELETE_TRIPS
CREATE_TRIP_REPORT, DELETE_TRIP_COMMENTS
BYPASS_LEVEL_REQ, OVERRIDE_WAITLIST_SETTING
VIEW_TRIPS_AS_LEAD, CAN_BE_DEPUTY_LEAD
CREATE_MEETING_POINTS, EDIT_MEETING_POINTS, DELETE_MEETING_POINTS
CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_SELF, CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_OTHERS
APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ, VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ
VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ, EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ, DELETE_UPGRADE_REQ
CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ, DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ
CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES, SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS, CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER
VIEW_CONTACT_INFO, VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY, SEARCH_MEMBERS, SEARCH_TRIPS
EDIT_MEMBERSHIP_PAYMENTS, EDIT_GLOBAL_SETTINGS, EDIT_UI_STRINGS, SEND_CLUB_NEWS
ACCESS_MARSHAL_PANEL, APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION

The full list lives in api/choices.py (ActionChoice).

docs.title: Custom permission classes
docs.text: api/permissions.py contains 30+ DRF permission classes that wrap PermissionMatrix.has_permission() for specific actions and viewsets. Reuse the existing class for your action before inventing a new one.

docs.title: Authority ranking
docs.text:
When docs disagree, trust in this order:

  1. Source code — ground truth for behaviour
  2. infra/.env.example — ground truth for environment variables
  3. schema.yml — ground truth for API surface (auto-generated)
  4. AGENTS.md — load-bearing rules and gotchas
  5. docs/ai-context/*.md — domain reference (this file)
  6. docs/*.md — MkDocs human docs
  7. README.md — public front door

docs.title: Deployment, Environment & Disaster Recovery
docs.text:
AI-context reference. Hetzner deployment, Docker stack, env-var inventory, host monitoring, and the DR runbook summary.

Authoritative operational docs: - infra/README.txt — step-by-step deployment / redeploy runbook (docker build, SSL, DB migrations, FCM path) - infra/.env.example — canonical environment-variable template; ground truth. The list in this file mirrors it but may lag — always verify against .env.example and update both in the same PR when adding a variable. - infra/disaster-recovery/Disaster-README.md — full DR setup + restore procedures.

docs.title: Docker stack (production, via infra/docker-compose.yml)
docs.text:
nginx          ← SSL termination, static files, reverse proxy
postgres       ← Primary database
redis          ← Cache + Huey broker
bugsink-db     ← Dedicated Bugsink Postgres database
bugsink        ← Self-hosted Sentry-compatible error tracker
app            ← Gunicorn (Django), built from Dockerapp
huey           ← Huey consumer, built from Dockerhuey

Hosted on Hetzner. Images are Docker multi-stage Python 3.13 builds.

docs.title: Error tracking — Bugsink
docs.text:
Bugsink is the production exception target. Django + Huey use sentry-sdk with DjangoIntegration, HueyIntegration, and RedisIntegration when SENTRY_DSN is set. The DSN points at the Bugsink project; the env var keeps the Sentry-compatible name on purpose.

django.request logs always go to console. AdminEmailHandler 500 emails are enabled when SENTRY_DSN is blank; once Bugsink is configured, they're disabled unless DJANGO_ENABLE_ADMIN_ERROR_EMAIL=true overrides. Operational emails (backup-failure, disk-space) stay on their own channel.

Sentry SDK is configured not to send request bodies or local frame variables. A before_send hook scrubs common secret-bearing keys, URL query parameters, and key=value breadcrumb strings before they leave the app.

The default compose deployment keeps Bugsink internal to the Docker network and binds the UI to 127.0.0.1:${BUGSINK_HOST_PORT:-18000} on the host for SSH-tunneled admin access. BUGSINK_BASE_URL should stay set to that admin-accessible URL. Backend ingestion uses a SENTRY_DSN whose host resolves inside Docker (usually bugsink:8000). With the default localhost URL, Bugsink-generated email links are only useful from the VPS or via SSH tunnel; configure a real HTTPS URL before using Bugsink email features.

docs.title: Disaster Recovery
docs.text:
Lives under infra/disaster-recovery/. Three files:

  • backup.sh — orchestrates backups of the PostgreSQL database, user uploads, source code, and infra config. Runs under flock so overlapping cron invocations are safe. Builds into /home/admin/backups/staging/ and atomically promotes to /home/admin/backups/latest/ only after a successful run, so a failed backup never leaves the server with zero local copies. Writes /home/admin/backups/backup-status.json after every run (for monitoring) and rotates its log via /etc/logrotate.d/ad4x4-backup. Bugsink issue data is treated as disposable operational telemetry and is not backed up; infra/bugsink-db-data/ and infra/db-data/ (live PostgreSQL data directory) are excluded from infra archives — the database is already captured via pg_dump. The Restic B2 repository is auto-initialised on first run if not found; a warning is added and the Restic step is skipped for that run if initialisation fails.
  • restore.sh — restores a backup to a fresh (or existing) Ubuntu host. Sources: gdrive, koofr, restic, or local. Restore order is source → infra → uploads → database — preserving this order is mandatory, otherwise the source-code extraction (rm -rf $APP_DIR) will wipe out already-restored infra and uploads. Handles both db.sql.gz (current) and db.sql (legacy) dumps. Discovers the postgres container name dynamically.
  • Disaster-README.md — setup instructions, fresh-VM quick restore, manual restore procedures.

docs.title: Backup targets and retention
docs.text:
Target Tool Snapshots kept Google Drive (gdrive:ad4x4-backups) rclone 2 most-recent snapshots + incremental uploads sync Koofr (koofr:ad4x4-backups) rclone 2 most-recent snapshots + incremental uploads sync Backblaze B2 (b2:hetzner-ad4x4:/restic-backups) restic 24 hourly / 3 daily / 2 weekly / 1 monthly (encrypted) Local plain filesystem 1 (latest/ only — no timestamped local folders)

Schedule: every 6 hours via cron (infra/disaster-recovery/crontab-example.txt).

docs.title: Critical DR gotchas
docs.text:
• Restic encrypts on B2, but Google Drive and Koofr receive plaintext db.sql.gz and tarballs. Anyone with access to those accounts can read everything.
  • The source-code archive is created with tar -C /home/admin ad4x4, so its entries begin with ad4x4/. On restore it must be extracted to $(dirname "$APP_DIR") (= /home/admin), not $APP_DIR itself — otherwise files land at /home/admin/ad4x4/ad4x4/....
  • restore.sh local always uses $BACKUP_ROOT/latest regardless of any timestamp argument, because the backup script no longer retains timestamped local copies.
  • Changing pg_dump output format requires updating restore.sh at the same time — both sides must agree on db.sql.gz vs db.sql vs -Fc custom format.
  • Migration 0085 (migrate_car_fields_to_vehicles) is effectively one-way. Its reverse_migration references Member.car_brand/car_model/car_year/car_color/car_image — columns that the subsequent migration 0086 removes. Rolling back past 0085 after 0086+ has applied will fail with AttributeError. If a rollback past this point is ever needed, restore the database from backup rather than running migrate --backwards.

docs.title: Host monitoring
docs.text: infra/monitoring/check-disk-space.sh is a host-level cron script for Hetzner VPS disk-space alerts. It parses only the needed keys from /home/admin/ad4x4/infra/.env, checks DISK_ALERT_PATHS, and sends email via the host mail command to DISK_ALERT_EMAIL or BACKUP_NOTIFY_EMAIL. Defaults alert at 85% usage or less than 2GB free, and suppress repeated emails for 6 hours while the condition remains active. The recommended cron entry is in infra/disaster-recovery/crontab-example.txt, which also creates /home/admin/monitoring before running.

docs.title: Maintenance mode
docs.text: Nginx-level 503 gate with admin-URI bypass; an optional API bypass allows either a bot-managed external IP whitelist match or the configured secret header. Wired up via MAINTENANCE_BYPASS_* env vars; the monitor bot can manage the bypass files at runtime when given the right privileges.

docs.title: Dev Setup, Testing & Commands
docs.text: AI-context reference. Local dev environment, test recipes, and the day-to-day commands. The MkDocs human walkthrough lives at docs/quick-start.md.

docs.title: First-time setup
docs.text:
# Virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate          # Unix
# venv\Scripts\activate            # Windows

# Dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt

# Database
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py createsuperuser

# Run
python manage.py runserver

# Background tasks (separate terminal)
python manage.py run_huey

Swagger UI is at http://localhost:8000/docs/swagger-ui/ once the server is running. MkDocs preview: mkdocs serve.

docs.title: Quick command reference
docs.text:
Task Command Run dev server python manage.py runserver Run background tasks python manage.py run_huey Run all tests python -m pytest tests api/tests Run with coverage python -m pytest --cov api tests api/tests Create migrations python manage.py makemigrations Apply migrations python manage.py migrate Regenerate OpenAPI schema python manage.py spectacular --file schema.yml Build docs mkdocs build Sync member level groups (backfill) python manage.py sync_member_level_groups

Prefer .venv/bin/python (Unix) or venv\Scripts\python.exe (Windows) when the local venv exists — the system Python in some shells does not include the project dependencies.

docs.title: Testing with PostgreSQL
docs.text:
• Framework: pytest + pytest-django with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=ad4x4.settings.
  • Before running tests, unset DJANGO_SECRET_KEY. If it's set, Django switches into production mode and expects the PG_POSTGRES_* settings, Redis, SSL, and production-like services.
  • pytest.ini pins testpaths = tests api/tests so collection doesn't wander into infra/db-data or other runtime folders.
  • Tests run against a local PostgreSQL instance via DEV_DB_* env vars. The configured Postgres user must be able to create and drop test databases; the default Docker postgres user is sufficient.

docs.title: Lightweight README dev container
docs.text:
Start it with docker start ad4x4-postgres and:

unset DJANGO_SECRET_KEY REDIS_HOST REDIS_PORT REDIS_PASSWORD
export DEV_DB_ENGINE=django.db.backends.postgresql
export DEV_DB_DATABASE=dev
export DEV_DB_USER=postgres
export DEV_DB_PASSWORD=postgres
export DEV_DB_HOST=localhost
export DEV_DB_PORT=5432
python -m pytest tests api/tests

docs.title: Full infra/docker-compose.yml stack
docs.text: Start the postgres service. Map PG_POSTGRES_DATABASE / PG_POSTGRES_USER / PG_POSTGRES_PASSWORD from infra/.env into DEV_DB_DATABASE / DEV_DB_USER / DEV_DB_PASSWORD. Use DEV_DB_PORT=15432.

docs.title: WSL local-development
docs.text: The repo's current .env exposes PostgreSQL on localhost:15432 with the credentials in infra/.env.

docs.title: Test naming convention
docs.text:
tests/test_<feature>.py — e.g., test_trips.py, test_members.py, test_logbook.py.

Run before every commit. Coverage: pytest --cov api. Shared fixtures live in test_util/ — TestData factory creates standard test objects (members, levels, trips, upgrade requests, logbook entries, etc.).

docs.title: Adding a new resource — checklist
docs.text:
1. Add model to api/models/<name>.py, register in api/models/__init__.py
  2. Create migration: python manage.py makemigrations
  3. Add serializer to api/serializers/serializers_<name>.py
  4. Add view to api/views/views_<name>.py
  5. Register ViewSet in ad4x4/urls.py
  6. Add PermissionMatrix.has_permission() checks
  7. Put business logic in api/services/, not the view
  8. Add Huey task to api/background.py if async work is needed
  9. Register in api/admin.py
  10. Add @extend_schema decorators for Swagger docs
  11. Write tests in tests/test_<name>.py (unless a closer api/tests/ home exists)
  12. Document in docs/<name>.md and add to mkdocs.yml
  13. Update docs/ai-context/*.md per the AGENTS.md self-update rule (only the file whose authoritative content changed)
  14. Regenerate schema.yml

docs.title: Agent / Claude Code preferences
docs.text:
• Do not commit automatically. Prompt when changes are ready and wait for explicit approval before git commit.
  • Always run tests before declaring done.
  • No comments unless requested. Follow existing code style.
  • Use existing serializers / views / services before introducing new ones.
  • Regenerate schema.yml after any endpoint change and commit it.

docs.title: Machine-specific config
docs.text: Per-user paths (custom venv locations, machine-specific environment variables) belong in your local Claude Code / Codex config (e.g. .claude/settings.local.json or shell rc), not in checked-in files.

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
AI-context reference. schema.yml (root) is the canonical source — auto-generated by python manage.py spectacular --file schema.yml after any endpoint change. This file is a navigable summary grouped by resource; if it disagrees with schema.yml, schema.yml wins.

All endpoints are under /api/. Authentication header: Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>. Response envelope and pagination rules: see architecture.md.

docs.title: Authentication (/api/auth/)
docs.text: Method Path Description POST /api/auth/login/ Login by login/username/email + password. Returns {access, refresh} wrapped in the unified envelope. Implemented by api.views.views_auth.LoginView, mounted before rest_registration's URLs so it shadows them. POST /api/auth/logout/ Body: {"refresh": "<token>"}. Blacklists only that single session. Idempotent. POST /api/auth/logout-all/ Blacklists every outstanding refresh token for the user (all devices, current included). GET /api/auth/sessions/ Lists the authenticated user's outstanding (non-blacklisted) refresh-token sessions (jti, created_at, expires_at only — never the raw token). DELETE /api/auth/sessions/ Body: {"keep_refresh": "<current session refresh token>"} (optional). Blacklists every session except the one whose refresh token is supplied. Without keep_refresh behaves like logout-all. POST /api/auth/register/ Register new member (rest_registration) POST /api/auth/register-email/ Register / change an email address POST /api/auth/verify-email/ Verify an email address POST /api/auth/verify-registration/ Verify email (rest_registration) POST /api/auth/reset-password/ Reset password (rest_registration) POST /api/auth/send-reset-password-link/ Send reset email POST /api/auth/change-password/ Change password. Blacklists every outstanding refresh token for the user — see gotchas. GET/PUT/PATCH /api/auth/profile/ Member profile (rest_registration) GET/PUT/PATCH /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings Notification preferences POST /api/token/ Alias for /api/auth/login/ POST /api/token/refresh/ Exchange a refresh token for a new {access, refresh} pair. Refresh tokens rotate — see gotchas.

/search, /lead-trip-history /<pk>/register, /<pk>/unregister, /<pk>/removemember, /<pk>/waitlist /<pk>/addfromwaitlist, /<pk>/forceregister /<pk>/approve, /<pk>/decline /<pk>/checkin, /<pk>/checkout /<pk>/comments, /<pk>/tripreports /<pk>/exportregistrants (CSV download) /<pk>/viewlogbooks, /<pk>/logbook-entries

docs.title: Two-step overlap guard
docs.text: Trip create/register/waitlist have a two-step overlap guard. If the chosen lead or registering member has an approved or pending overlapping trip where they are registered or primary lead, the first request returns 409 with message: "trip_overlap_warning" and structured warnings; no mutation happens. Clients retry the same request with confirmOverlap: true to proceed. Waitlist-only and deputy-lead roles do not count as conflicts; exact boundary-touching times do not overlap.

docs.title: External Services
docs.text:
AI-context reference. Wire-up for each integration plus what holds the credentials.

Service Purpose Config location Firebase FCM Push notifications FCM_SERVICE_KEY_PATH env var; fcm_django in INSTALLED_APPS Telegram Bot Admin-facing notifications, host-monitor bot, GitHub PR alerts TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID env vars; topic-specific thread IDs documented in deployment.md HERE Maps Reverse geocoding ConfigurableSettings.here_maps_* fields. apiKey is a request parameter — keep API errors generic and avoid logging full request URLs so the key is not exposed in responses or logs. Gallery API Trip photo albums GALLERY_API_BASE_URL + GALLERY_API_TOKEN env vars; ConfigurableSettings.gallery_* fields. Tasks retry up to 6× with 1-hour delays — see services-and-tasks.md. PayPal Membership payments PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID + PAYPAL_SECRET_KEY env vars; PayPalConfiguration model (singleton). PayPal does not support AED — charges USD, displays AED. Bugsink (Sentry-compatible) Error tracking SENTRY_DSN env var (intentionally keeps the Sentry variable name but points at the Bugsink project DSN). bugsink service in infra/docker-compose.yml. Sentry SDK is configured not to send request bodies or local frame variables; a before_send hook scrubs common secret-bearing keys, URL query parameters, and key=value breadcrumb strings before they leave the app. Gmail SMTP Transactional email EMAIL_HOST_USER + EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD env vars

docs.title: Routine 500 emails vs Bugsink
docs.text: django.request logs always go to console. AdminEmailHandler 500 emails are enabled when SENTRY_DSN is blank. Once Bugsink is configured, they are disabled unless DJANGO_ENABLE_ADMIN_ERROR_EMAIL=true explicitly re-enables them. Operational emails (backup-failure alerts, disk-space alerts) are a separate channel and remain.

docs.title: Data Models
docs.text: AI-context reference. Models live in api/models/ (one file per model group, registered in api/models/__init__.py). The website app contributes two singleton-style models. Always read AGENTS.md first for the gotchas that touch these models.

docs.title: api.Member — AUTHUSERMODEL
docs.text:
Custom AbstractUser. Key fields: - username (unique, 50) - email (unique, 255) - phone (PhoneNumberField, AE region) - level (FK → Level) - trip_count - gender (M/F/O) - nationality (ISO 3166 code) - avatar (ImageField, max 2.5MB) - paid_member (bool) - token_version (legacy column, no longer used for JWT invalidation — see gotchas) - last_visited (DateTimeField, updated by LastVisitedMiddleware throttled 1/hr)

Manager: MyUserManager — case-insensitive get_by_natural_key. Key method: anonymize_data() — GDPR deletion (deactivates, wipes PII, deletes vehicles). Level-group sync: enforced in api.signals.member_post_save via sync_member_level_groups(). Backfill command: python manage.py sync_member_level_groups.

docs.title: Level
docs.text: name, numeric_level (1–999), auto_group (FK → Group; auto-assigns users on upgrade), display_name, active, min_trips_for_upgrade.

docs.title: PermissionMatrix
docs.text:
Group-based permission control. Fields: action (ActionChoice), group (FK → Group), levels (M2M → Level — empty means ALL levels, see gotchas). Unique on (action, group).

Class method: PermissionMatrix.has_permission(user, action, member=None, trip=None, require_trip_lead=False) — the authoritative permission check. Always use this for authorisation logic.

docs.title: Trip
docs.text: lead (FK → Member, PROTECT), deputy_leads (M2M → Member), title, description, level (FK → Level, PROTECT), start_time, end_time, cut_off, meeting_point (FK → MeetingPoint), capacity, registered (M2M via TripRegistration), waitlist (M2M via TripWaitlist), approval_status (P/A/R/C), allow_waitlist, gallery_id (UUID string, links to external gallery service).

docs.title: TripRegistration / TripWaitlist
docs.text:
Join tables with member, trip, vehicle (optional FK, SET_NULL on vehicle delete), registration_date, checked_in (TripRegistration only).

Trip detail responses may also include overlap metadata on each registered[] row: hasOverlap and overlappingTrips. Those use the same overlap rules as the create/register/waitlist warnings and are intended for trip-lead roster review.

docs.title: TripRegistrationCancellationReason
docs.text: Audit record for lead/admin cancellation actions. Stores the affected member, trip, optional vehicle, cancellation reason, and whether the member came from registered or waitlist state. Notification tasks take this row's id, not model instances.

docs.title: TripComment / TripRating
docs.text: Trip discussion and rating records. TripComment drives comment notifications; TripRating stores member feedback for completed trips.

docs.title: TripRequest
docs.text: Member's trip wish: member, time_of_day (MOR/MID/AFT/EVE/ANY), area (DXB/NOR/AUH/AAN/LIW), level, date (max 16 days ahead). Auto-deleted after 1 day by periodic task.

docs.title: UpgradeRequest
docs.text:
applicant (FK → Member, nullable — store username backup in applicant_str), target_level, status (N/I/A/D), yes_voters/no_voters/defer_voters/nominated_voters (all M2M → Member), final_approver, verdict_date, verdict_reason, attachment.

Status flow: NEW → IN_PROGRESS → APPROVED/DECLINED. verdict_date auto-set in save().

docs.title: UpgradeRequestComment
docs.text: Comment thread on upgrade requests. Create/edit/delete actions are PermissionMatrix-gated separately from the parent request.

docs.title: LogbookSkill / LogbookSkillCategory
docs.text: Skills that can be verified on trips. name, description, active, level_requirement (FK → Level), order, count_requirement, category (FK → LogbookSkillCategory).

docs.title: LogbookEntry
docs.text: Trip attendance + skill record per member. trip, member, signed_by (marshal), skills_verified (M2M → LogbookSkill), comment. Unique per (member, trip) so migration approval reuses the same parent row instead of creating duplicates.

docs.title: LogbookSkillReference
docs.text: Granular join: member earned a specific skill on a specific trip. logbook_skill, member, trip, signed_by, entered_by, entered_at. Unique on (member, trip, logbook_skill) — preserves audit history (see gotchas).

docs.title: LogbookMigrationRequest
docs.text: Import logbook from old system. member, target_level, status (PENDING/APPROVED/RETURNED/REJECTED), migration_type (MEMBERINITIATED/MANAGERDIRECT), uploaded_pdf, rejection_reason, return_comment. Create-time validation rejects duplicate skill_entries.trip values with migration_skill_entries_duplicate_trip.

docs.title: LogbookMigrationSkillEntry
docs.text: Per-skill entry attached to a migration request. Records requested migrated skill evidence before approval.

docs.title: ClubNews
docs.text: Broadcast to members at specific levels. title, content, levels (M2M, empty=all), status (DRAFT→APPROVED→SENT/ERROR), image. SENT records are immutable — save() raises ValidationError on modification attempts (see gotchas).

docs.title: NotificationLog
docs.text: Notification audit trail. member, title, body, timestamp, type (NotificationType), related_object_id, related_object_type, is_read. Purged after 60 days by a periodic task.

docs.title: GitHubWebhookDelivery
docs.text: Inbound GitHub webhook audit trail for private-repo PR notifications. Tracks delivery_id, repository, event_name, action, PR metadata, delivery status, payload, error, and timestamps.

docs.title: NotificationSettings
docs.text: Per-member notification preferences for email/push/Telegram-style delivery channels. Created alongside members and touched by the legacy auth side effect in JWTAuthentication.get_user().

docs.title: ConfigurableSettings (singleton)
docs.text:
Global configuration. One record only — save() raises on duplicate. Includes: default user level/group, auto-upgrade rules, email addresses, email sleep period, notification dry-run toggle, HERE Maps config, gallery API config, vehicle limit per member, force_waitlist, trip edit cutoff minutes.

Always access via ConfigurableSettings.objects.first() or the global_settings.py service. .objects.first() can return None in fresh dev/test environments where the row hasn't been seeded — guard for None or use the service.

docs.title: GeocodingCache
docs.text: HERE Maps response cache. Unique on (latitude, longitude). Has expires_at, increment_access(), cleanup_expired() class method. Periodic task cleans stale entries at 1 AM.

docs.title: Vehicle
docs.text: Member's vehicle. brand (74 CarBrand choices), model, year, color, image, is_primary. Limit enforced by vehicle_limit_per_member in ConfigurableSettings.

docs.title: AccountDeletionRequest
docs.text: 3-day grace period model. Midnight periodic task calls member.anonymize_data() and deletes the request.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: Member feedback/contact submission with optional images and admin notification side effects.

docs.title: Sponsorship
docs.text: Sponsor directory entry with logo/image and ordering/display metadata.

docs.title: FaqEntry
docs.text: Public FAQ entry, ordered for client display.

docs.title: TripReport / TripReportImage
docs.text: Post-trip reports and their images. Trip reports are exposed as a nested trip resource and as a separate report list.

docs.title: UIString
docs.text: Admin-managed key/value strings used by clients for dynamic copy.

docs.title: PayPalConfiguration (website app, singleton)
docs.text: Payment config: sandbox_mode, is_active, payment_amount / payment_currency (PayPal-side, limited currency list), display_amount / display_currency (shown to user, AED). PayPal does NOT support AED — the club charges in USD (~27 USD) but shows 100 AED. See gotchas.

docs.title: WebsitePayment (website app)
docs.text: Transaction record: member, amount, currency, payment_method, paypal_order_id, paypal_transaction_id, payer_email, status (pending/completed/failed/refunded).

docs.title: Services Layer & Background Tasks
docs.text: AI-context reference. Views must be thin. All business logic lives in api/services/. Async work is done by Huey, defined in api/background.py.

docs.title: Services (api/services/)
docs.text:
Service file Responsibility notification_service.py Orchestrates all notification sending (email + push + Telegram) push_notifications.py FCM push notification delivery email_notifications.py SMTP email composition and delivery telegram_notifications.py Telegram bot messages store_notifications.py Saves NotificationLog records init_notifications.py Notification setup / initialization trip_registration_service.py Trip register / unregister / waitlist business rules upgrade_eligibility.py Checks if member is eligible for level upgrade auto_upgrade_service.py Automatic upgrade on logbook completion gallery_webhook.py Creates / updates / deletes galleries in the external media service global_settings.py Convenient access to ConfigurableSettings singleton here_maps_service.py Reverse geocoding with cache permission_service.py Permission-related helpers

Reuse the existing service for a given concern before introducing a new one. If a new service is needed, name it <resource>_service.py and register it under api/services/__init__.py if you want it importable from api.services.

docs.title: Huey background tasks
docs.text:
Huey runs as a separate Docker container (Dockerhuey) in production, consuming from Redis. In development (no DJANGO_SECRET_KEY), tasks run synchronously (immediate mode) — see gotchas.

Define tasks in api/background.py. Enqueue them from inside a DB write path with transaction.on_commit(lambda: task(pk)) and pass primitive ids, not model instances — see gotchas.

docs.title: Async tasks (event-triggered)
docs.text: Task Trigger Retries send_trip_notification Trip published 2 retries, 5 min delay send_trip_approval_notification Trip approved / declined 2 retries, 5 min delay send_registration_from_waitlist_notification Member moved from waitlist 2 retries, 15 min delay send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification Member removed from trip 2 retries, 15 min delay send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification Member removed from waitlist 2 retries, 15 min delay send_upgrade_request_handled_notification Upgrade request approved / declined 2 retries, 5 min delay send_upgrade_request_created_notification New upgrade request 2 retries, 5 min delay send_club_news ClubNews status → APPROVED 2 retries, 5 min delay send_feedback_notification Feedback submitted 2 retries, 5 min delay send_new_trip_comment_notification_task New trip comment 2 retries, 5 min delay create_gallery_for_trip_task Trip approved 6 retries, 1 hr delay update_gallery_for_trip_task Trip edited 6 retries, 1 hr delay delete_gallery_for_trip_task Trip deleted 3 retries, 1 hr delay restore_gallery_for_trip_task Trip restored 3 retries, 1 hr delay

docs.title: Periodic tasks (cron)
docs.text: Schedule Task Action Daily 00:00 process_account_deletion_requests Anonymize members who requested deletion >3 days ago Daily 01:00 cleanup_expired_geocoding_cache Delete expired HERE Maps cache entries Daily 02:00 periodic_purge_inactive_devices Delete inactive FCM devices >30 days Daily 03:00 periodic_delete_old_triprequests Delete TripRequest rows older than yesterday Daily 04:00 periodic_purge_old_notifications Delete NotificationLog rows >60 days Daily 04:30 cleanup_blacklisted_tokens Delete BlacklistedToken rows whose underlying refresh has already expired Daily 04:45 cleanup_expired_outstanding_tokens Delete OutstandingToken rows whose refresh has expired (cascades blacklist rows) Daily 20:00 periodic_upgrade_request_reminder Send upgrade request reminders
